text:
incident-bot: PAGER: Tokenizer/preproc latency SLO breach detected for route /v1/chat/stream (p99 > 1.2s). Severity: potential user impact. Paging on-call.
Amber (oncall): ACK. I'm on it, grabbing metrics and traces.
Sam (eng-runtime): I'm seeing a sharp tail on tokenization step starting ~16:03 UTC. p95 ~420ms -> p95 normal ~120ms, p99 ~1.6s. Streaming stalls at the preproc handoff (frames show backlog).
Maria (eng-sre): Linking dashboards: https://internal.redwood/dashboards/preproc-latency?range=15m. There's a correlated CPU spike on preproc workers.
Kevin (eng-ml): Noticed an uptick in JSON-mode parse time for long templates. Example: template with nested tool schema + large system prompt triggers expensive parsing loop.
Olivia (support): We have 3 open customer tickets mentioning slow streaming and partial responses: #1421 (Acme), #1422 (BrightHealth), #1423 (EdgeChat). Customers reporting timeouts and partial messages mid-stream.
Amber (oncall): Is this isolated to a model shard or global? Any recent deploys to preproc?
Sam (eng-runtime): No deploys flagged. Heatmap shows most errors on region-us-west-2 and dedicated-pool-3. Tokenizer logs (excerpt):
```
[16:04:12] worker-12 tokenizer_ms=482 template_parse_ms=210 jsonmode_ms=180 queue_wait_ms=95
[16:04:13] worker-07 tokenizer_ms=510 template_parse_ms=230 jsonmode_ms=190 queue_wait_ms=120
[16:04:14] ERROR preproc.handoff timeout after 120s for request id=...
```
Amber (oncall): Ok, plan: 1) mitigate obvious customer impact (route streaming to safe fallback), 2) isolate root cause (template/jsonmode heavy paths), 3) restore SLOs.
Maria (eng-sre): I'm going to patch the ingress routing rule to send traffic for /v1/chat/stream to the fallback preproc pool for 5 mins. Command: `redwoodctl route update --path /v1/chat/stream --pool preproc-fallback --duration 5m` — doing it now.
Sam (eng-runtime): Suggest also flipping feature flag `enable_json_mode` -> false for streaming routes until we confirm parser fix. That will avoid expensive JSON schema assembly.
Kevin (eng-ml): Be aware disabling JSON mode will change a few tool schema responses, but it's safer. We should notify product/support.
Lisa (product): Noted. I'll draft customer-facing blurb: "Temporarily disabling structured JSON mode for streaming to mitigate latency. No loss of core content expected; structured tooling calls may be delayed"
Maria (eng-sre): Route change applied at 16:07 UTC. Observability: p99 down to ~580ms within ~90s. Streaming error rate dropping.
Olivia (support): Notifying affected customers in the tickets now. Ticket updates sent to Acme and BrightHealth.
Sam (eng-runtime): Rolling a quick config to set `preproc.workers=auto` -> increases preproc concurrency by +30% in affected pools. Command: `kubectl -n preproc set env deployment/preproc PREPROC_WORKERS=auto` (applied).
Amber (oncall): Monitoring CPU and queue lengths. If CPU spikes further, we'll scale-out instead of further tuning.
Kevin (eng-ml): Quick reproduction note: send a large prompt with nested tool schema and JSON-mode true, should reproduce parse hotspot. I'll open a small repro harness in /eng-ml/incidents.
Sam (eng-runtime): Adding short-term guard: drop templates over 12k chars for streaming path and fall back to chunked render. Patch pushed: `if len(template) > 12000: chunk_render()` — rolling.
Maria (eng-sre): At 16:12 UTC p95 back to ~160ms, p99 ~250ms, error rate normalized. Customer-facing metric: streaming timeouts down 93%.
Amber (oncall): Declaring "mitigated" at 16:13 UTC. Continuing to monitor for 30m.
Lisa (product): Thanks. I'll coordinate release notes and a small heads-up to enterprise accounts.
Olivia (support): Customers updated, closing the urgent P1 threads on our side.
Kevin (eng-ml): Root cause hypothesis: expensive JSON-mode assembly combined with some unusually large tool-schema templates caused O(n^2) behavior in the template parser, which then amplified queue wait and blocked streaming handoffs. Will prepare a patch to optimize parser and add complexity guards.
Sam (eng-runtime): Follow-ups for postmortem: 1) add automated test with nested tool schemas to CI, 2) add a complexity limiter in the tokenizer/preproc, 3) improve fallback routing automation (so route update can be triggered automatically when p99 > threshold), 4) add alert for sustained template_parse_ms > 200ms.
Maria (eng-sre): I'll file the incident and assign owners. Incident link: https://incidents.redwood/2380000123. Severity updated to Sev2 (SLO breach, multiple customers impacted, mitigated).
Amber (oncall): Thanks team. Quick notes: blameless, focus on fixes and customer communication. I'll run the on-call handoff summary to next shift.
Lisa (product): Tagging Sales for enterprise outreach: @sales-team. Also coordinating a small compensation package for the top affected customers.
Kevin (eng-ml): I'll open a PR with parser optimizations and unit tests.
Sam (eng-runtime): I'll add a runtime guard and an automated route fallback playbook.
Maria (eng-sre): Postmortem ETA: EOD tomorrow. Will include timelines, impact, and remediation steps.
Olivia (support): Closing internal support loop for now; will reopen if any customers report regressions.
Amber (oncall): Closing thread summary: mitigated at 16:13 UTC, monitoring window in effect until 16:43 UTC, owners: Kevin (parser fix), Sam (runtime guards & routing automation), Maria (postmortem & alerting), Lisa/Olivia (customer comms). Thanks everyone. :tada:
